easy.def: One of the four parts of the year.
examples: Winter is the cold season.
What season is your birthday in?
Summer is the hot season.

more.def: One of the four parts of the year: spring, summer, fall, and winter.
examples: Fall is my favorite season because the leaves change color.
Soccer season starts in the spring.
Strawberries are in season in early summer.
I am in second grade.
She came in second place.
This is my second try.

more.def: Coming right after the first in order.
examples: The second runner crossed the line just after the first.
Turn to the second page of the book.
This is my second visit to the aquarium.

easy.def: A very short bit of time.
examples: Wait a second.
It took one second.
I will be back in a second.

more.def: A very short period of time, and one sixtieth of a minute.
examples: There are sixty seconds in a minute.
Wait a second while I tie my shoe.
The runner finished one second before her friend.

easy.def: Something you do not tell other people.
examples: The gift is a secret.
Can you keep a secret?
I have a secret hiding spot.

more.def: Something that is kept hidden or known by only a few people.
examples: She kept the surprise party a secret for two weeks.
The recipe is a family secret.
He whispered the secret to his best friend.

easy.def: To use your eyes to look at something.
examples: I see a bird.
She saw a rainbow.
Can you see the moon?

more.def: To notice something with your eyes, or to understand something.
examples: From the top of the hill, we could see the whole town.
I see what you mean about the math problem.
He has never seen snow before.

easy.def: To look or feel a certain way.
examples: You seem sad.
It seems cold.
He seemed happy.

more.def: To give the feeling of being a certain way, though it may not be true.
examples: The night seems quiet when it snows.
She seemed nervous before the big spelling bee.
The test did not seem hard to me.
It is selfish not to share.
The selfish cat took the whole bed.
Do not be selfish with the ball.

more.def: Caring only about yourself and not about other people.
examples: It was selfish of him to eat the whole cake without sharing.
A selfish player never passes the ball.
She realized it was selfish to keep the window seat every time.

easy.def: To make something go to another place.
examples: I send a card.
She sent a letter.
Mom sends me to school.

more.def: To make something go to another place, or to tell someone to go.
examples: I will send a postcard to my grandmother from the beach.
The teacher sent a note home with each student.
The coach sent the players onto the field.

easy.def: To put something in a place.
examples: Set the cup down.
I set the table.
She set the box here.

more.def: To put something in a certain place or position, or to get it ready.
examples: Please set the vase on the shelf.
He set the alarm clock for seven.
We set the table before dinner.

easy.def: A group of things that go together.
examples: I have a set of blocks.
A set of crayons.
She has a tea set.

more.def: A group of things that belong together.
examples: I got a set of paints for my birthday.
The library has a whole set of books about space.
He keeps a set of tools in the garage.
